sec04-card-f09.question_text: Which two shapes and three background colors may roadway guide signs use?
sec04-card-f09.teaching_text: Matching green to directions, blue to services, and brown to recreation speeds up highway decision-making.

sec04-card-f10.question_text: What four categories of travel information do guide signs display?
sec04-card-f10.teaching_text: Advance navigation boards let you line up your lane calmly miles before an unfamiliar junction arrives.

sec04-card-f11.question_text: Which four motorist needs can service guide signs point you toward?
sec04-card-f11.teaching_text: Checking blue roadside panels before exiting prevents aimless detours when fuel runs low or emergencies strike.

sec04-card-f12.question_text: What do a route-number sign's shape and color tell a driver?
sec04-card-f12.teaching_text: Recognizing interstate shields versus federal, Ohio state, or county outlines confirms you are on the intended route.

sec04-card-f13.question_text: Which four visual forms can painted roadway markings take?
sec04-card-f13.teaching_text: Pavement graphics sit directly in your forward sightline so you never miss lane rules in heavy traffic.

sec04-card-f14.question_text: Which five traffic-control jobs do pavement markings perform?
sec04-card-f14.teaching_text: From dividing lanes to marking exact signal stop bars, painted markings organize every shared conflict point.

sec04-card-f15.question_text: What traffic flow do white lane lines separate, and what two styles do they take?
sec04-card-f15.teaching_text: Seeing white stripes on both sides confirms adjacent lanes travel your way rather than head-on.

sec04-card-f16.question_text: What traffic directions does a solid yellow pavement line separate?
sec04-card-f16.teaching_text: Yellow paint on your left warns constantly that oncoming bumpers sit immediately across that boundary.

sec04-card-r01.question_text: When is crossing left of double solid yellow centerlines permitted in Ohio?
sec04-card-r01.teaching_text: Ohio exams test this key twist where bikes or slow-emblem vehicles can be passed safely across double yellow.

sec04-card-r02.question_text: What does a solid-and-dashed yellow centerline pair allow when the dashed stripe is on your side?
sec04-card-r02.teaching_text: Having the broken stripe touching your lane confirms engineers verified forward sight distance for your direction.

sec04-card-r03.question_text: What rule applies when the solid stripe of a mixed yellow centerline sits on your side?
sec04-card-r03.teaching_text: A hill crest or curve ahead blocks your sightline even while oncoming traffic enjoys a clear view.

sec04-card-r04.question_text: Who may pass along a single dashed yellow centerline, and under what condition?
sec04-card-r04.teaching_text: Permission on paint never guarantees an empty lane, so verify long clear distance before pulling left.

sec04-card-r05.question_text: How is a shared two-way left-turn lane marked along its borders and pavement?
sec04-card-r05.teaching_text: Outer solid with inner dashed yellow lines paired with opposing white left arrows distinguish center turn lanes.

sec04-card-r06.question_text: When may drivers enter a shared two-way left-turn lane, and what two uses are banned?
sec04-card-r06.teaching_text: Cruising down a center turn lane to bypass backups or overtake cars creates head-on collisions.

sec04-card-r07.question_text: What roadway area does a crosswalk identify?
sec04-card-r07.teaching_text: Treating every crosswalk as protected pedestrian space prevents rolling stops that cut off people on foot.

sec04-card-r08.question_text: When must drivers yield to pedestrians at a crosswalk?
sec04-card-r08.teaching_text: You do not wait until a walker reaches your bumper; stepping into or crossing within triggers your yield.

sec04-card-r09.question_text: Where must you bring your vehicle to a halt when a stop line precedes a crosswalk?
sec04-card-r09.teaching_text: Stopping short of the painted bar keeps your hood out of the pedestrian path and protects cross visibility.

sec04-card-r10.question_text: Do all marked pedestrian crosswalks look identical on the pavement?
sec04-card-r10.teaching_text: Whether striped with parallel bars, ladder rungs, or diagonal hashes, every crosswalk style carries identical legal protection.

sec05-card-f01.question_text: Where should you look for a specific vehicle's exact starting instructions?
sec05-card-f01.teaching_text: Keyless push-buttons, hybrids, and traditional ignitions vary across models, making the owner's manual your authoritative reference.

sec05-card-f02.question_text: What foot, gear-selector, and ignition steps start the handbook's automatic vehicle?
sec05-card-f02.teaching_text: Holding the brake firmly in park prevents any unexpected roll the moment the engine fires.

sec05-card-f03.question_text: What sequence of gear, traffic checks, signal, and pedal steps moves you smoothly from a stop?
sec05-card-f03.teaching_text: Checking ahead, beside, and behind with your blinker on catches approaching cars or cyclists before you roll.

sec05-card-f04.question_text: How should you position your foot and heel to accelerate smoothly?
sec05-card-f04.teaching_text: Pivoting on your anchored heel gives smooth, fine-grained throttle control instead of jerky stomps.

sec05-card-f05.question_text: What three steps produce a controlled, normal stop?
sec05-card-f05.teaching_text: Glancing at your rearview mirror before braking warns you early if a distracted tailgater is closing fast.

sec05-card-f06.question_text: Which four human, speed, mechanical, and road factors determine total stopping distance?
sec05-card-f06.teaching_text: Worn brake pads, wet asphalt, slower alertness, or higher speed each stretch how far your car rolls.

sec05-card-f07.question_text: How many seconds of following space should you maintain behind the vehicle ahead?
sec05-card-f07.teaching_text: Counting seconds past a fixed landmark adjusts your physical following distance automatically as speeds climb.

sec05-card-f08.question_text: Where must your front bumper stop at a stop sign or steady red light?
sec05-card-f08.teaching_text: Rolling over the painted bar blocks pedestrian crossings and puts your bumper into cross-traffic turn arcs.

sec05-card-f09.question_text: What stop and yield duties still apply even when turning on red is allowed?
sec05-card-f09.teaching_text: Rolling through a right-on-red without a dead stop behind the line is a classic road-test failure.

sec05-card-f10.question_text: How must you handle an intersection controlled by a flashing red traffic light?
sec05-card-f10.teaching_text: Cross streets may face a flashing yellow rather than a stop, so never assume a four-way halt.

sec05-card-f11.question_text: Where must you stop and who gets priority when emerging from an alley or driveway in town?
sec05-card-f11.teaching_text: Fences and hedges hide joggers on the sidewalk until your nose stops short of the walkway.

sec05-card-f12.question_text: What must you do at a green signal when backed-up cars leave no room for your car on the far side?
sec05-card-f12.teaching_text: Pulling into a jammed intersection traps you broadside across cross traffic when the signal changes.

sec05-card-f13.question_text: What must you do for an approaching emergency vehicle with lights and siren, and what divided-road exception applies?
sec05-card-f13.teaching_text: Clearing right and stopping opens a clean lane, whereas an unbroken median separates opposite-side emergency runs.

sec05-card-f14.question_text: Which way do you turn the steering wheel to guide the car forward or in reverse?
sec05-card-f14.teaching_text: Wanting the rear bumper to swing right in reverse means turning the top of the wheel right.

sec05-card-f15.question_text: Where on the wheel and how firmly does the Ohio handbook instruct placing both hands?
sec05-card-f15.teaching_text: Holding four and eight on the outer rim steadies steering while keeping forearms clear of airbag deployment.

sec05-card-f16.question_text: Why should you check behind a parked vehicle before climbing into the driver's seat?
sec05-card-f16.teaching_text: Trunk lids and rear pillars create a deep blind zone that hides toddlers, pets, or toys completely.

sec05-card-f17.question_text: Where must your foot be while moving the gear selector into reverse?
sec05-card-f17.teaching_text: Pressing the service brake prevents sudden backward lurching the instant reverse gear engages.

sec05-card-f18.question_text: How should you position your hands, arm, and gaze when backing straight?
sec05-card-f18.teaching_text: Draping your right arm over the passenger seat rotates your torso for a direct view out the back glass.

sec05-card-f19.question_text: Why can't you rely solely on mirrors while backing up?
sec05-card-f19.teaching_text: Side and interior mirrors angle outward and over the trunk, leaving a blind pocket right behind your bumper.

sec05-card-f20.question_text: How should you use a rear-view backup camera, and why shouldn't you trust it alone?
sec05-card-f20.teaching_text: Wide-angle lenses still miss cross-traffic corners and dirty-lens spots that real head checks catch.

sec05-card-f21.question_text: How fast should you reverse, and how much wheel input should you use?
sec05-card-f21.teaching_text: Front-wheel steering swings the nose wide in reverse, making sharp corrections exaggerated and tricky at speed.

sec05-card-f22.question_text: Where must you look while backing through a turn until the car comes to a complete stop?
sec05-card-f22.teaching_text: Quick front-fender glances prevent scraping parked cars beside you while primary eyes stay rearward until stopped.

sec05-card-f23.question_text: What should you do with your speed and eyes at every approaching intersection?
sec05-card-f23.teaching_text: Checking controls, walkers, slick spots, and sightline blockers early prevents surprises inside the conflict zone.

sec05-card-f24.question_text: In what sequence should you scan for cars, motorcycles, and bicycles at an intersection?
sec05-card-f24.teaching_text: Your lane crosses left-approaching traffic first, so a second glance left catches fast bikes before pulling out.

sec05-card-f25.question_text: What three preparation steps belong ahead of making an intersection turn?
sec05-card-f25.teaching_text: Moving into the proper curb or center lane early prevents cutting across neighboring traffic mid-turn.

sec05-card-f26.question_text: Where should you aim your eyes while steering through a turn?
sec05-card-f26.teaching_text: Your hands naturally steer where your eyes lead, and looking deep into the target lane spots hazards early.

sec05-card-f27.question_text: What three steps finish a turn cleanly once your wheels straighten out?
sec05-card-f27.teaching_text: Matching traffic flow, making sure the blinker clicked off, and checking rear mirrors stabilizes your new lane.

sec05-card-f28.question_text: At least how far ahead of a turn must you signal, and what two methods are legal?
sec05-card-f28.teaching_text: Ohio knowledge exams test the exact one-hundred-foot minimum alongside knowing hand signals back up broken bulbs.

sec05-card-f29.question_text: What pre-turn steering error must passenger-car drivers avoid before turning right?
sec05-card-f29.teaching_text: Swinging left invites trailing drivers to think you are changing lanes left right before you cut back right.

sec05-card-f30.question_text: From where in your lane and into which part of the cross street should you turn right?
sec05-card-f30.teaching_text: Staying tight to the right curb keeps you from drifting wide into oncoming or parallel left lanes.

sec05-card-f31.question_text: To whom must a left-turning motorist yield before turning across the road?
sec05-card-f31.teaching_text: Misjudging oncoming speed during hurried left turns causes severe front-quarter intersection crashes.

sec05-card-f32.question_text: From which part of your lane and into which destination lane do you complete a left turn, including on four-lane roads?
sec05-card-f32.teaching_text: Swinging out into the right curb lane during a left turn collides with opposing right-turners legally entering it.

sec05-card-r01.question_text: How does the handbook describe positioning and yielding for a left turn on green when heavy opposing traffic blocks gaps?
sec05-card-r01.teaching_text: Keeping wheels straight just past the stop bar lets you clear safely once pedestrians and oncoming cars finish.

sec05-card-r02.question_text: How must you handle lane choice before and throughout a multi-lane turn?
sec05-card-r02.teaching_text: Drifting across dashed turn-guide arcs mid-intersection sideswipes the vehicle turning right beside you.

sec05-card-r03.question_text: Under what sign, stopping, and clearance conditions is a right turn on red legal?
sec05-card-r03.teaching_text: Check every corner for NO TURN ON RED plaques before stopping completely and yielding to walkers and cars.

sec05-card-r04.question_text: Between what exact street types and from which lane is a left turn on red legal unless prohibited?
sec05-card-r04.teaching_text: Turning left on red from or onto a two-way street crosses opposing lanes illegally and earns an instant fail.

sec05-card-r05.question_text: Why should you wait briefly rather than jackrabbiting out the instant a light turns green?
sec05-card-r05.teaching_text: Late red-light runners barrel through intersections during the first two seconds of cross-street green.

sec05-card-r06.question_text: When must you hold behind the stop line even though your signal is green?
sec05-card-r06.teaching_text: Waiting behind the crosswalk until a car-length opens ahead keeps cross traffic flowing when lights cycle.

sec05-card-r07.question_text: What three checks and actions belong to turning onto a busy roadway?
sec05-card-r07.teaching_text: Pulling into a tight gap and dawdling below traffic speed forces fast-approaching drivers to slam brakes.

sec05-card-r08.question_text: Why shouldn't you pull out right in front of an approaching car just because its turn signal is blinking?
sec05-card-r08.teaching_text: That driver may plan to turn into a driveway past you or forgot their blinker on miles ago.

sec05-card-r09.question_text: How should you handle a stop-sign intersection where parked cars, bushes, or buildings block cross visibility?
sec05-card-r09.teaching_text: Make your legal stop behind the line first, then inch forward slowly until you can see cross lanes.

sec05-card-r10.question_text: In which direction do vehicles travel around a roundabout's raised central island?
sec05-card-r10.teaching_text: Keeping the raised island on your left guides every entering stream smoothly to the right counterclockwise.

sec05-card-r11.question_text: Why must you read advance direction plaques before entering a multi-lane roundabout?
sec05-card-r11.teaching_text: Changing lanes inside the circular roadway is prohibited, so your approach lane locks in valid exits.

sec05-card-r12.question_text: What speed adjustment is required before entering a roundabout or traffic circle?
sec05-card-r12.teaching_text: Calm approach speeds give you time to judge circulating gaps and steer smoothly around tight radii.

sec05-card-r13.question_text: Who holds the right-of-way at a roundabout entrance?
sec05-card-r13.teaching_text: Vehicles already inside the ring always hold priority over drivers waiting at the dashed entry line.

sec05-card-r14.question_text: Which direction do you scan for circulating vehicles before entering a roundabout?
sec05-card-r14.teaching_text: Because roundabout traffic flows counterclockwise, every conflicting vehicle approaches exclusively from your left.

sec05-card-r15.question_text: Once inside a roundabout, what two things must you avoid doing?
sec05-card-r15.teaching_text: Stopping mid-circle to wave someone in causes immediate rear-end collisions behind you.

sec05-card-r16.question_text: What communication step is required as you reach your roundabout exit?
sec05-card-r16.teaching_text: Signaling your exit tells waiting drivers at the next leg they have a gap to enter.

sec05-card-r17.question_text: Which numbered exit in the handbook's standard roundabout pattern makes a right turn?
sec05-card-r17.teaching_text: Turning out at the immediate first leg completes a ninety-degree right turn without circling further.

sec05-card-r18.question_text: Which numbered exit in the handbook's standard roundabout pattern continues straight?
sec05-card-r18.teaching_text: Passing the right-hand leg and taking the second exit keeps you heading straight along your corridor.

sec05-card-r19.question_text: Which numbered exit in the handbook's standard roundabout pattern completes a left turn?
sec05-card-r19.teaching_text: Traveling three-quarters counterclockwise around the central island replaces a traditional left turn.

sec05-card-r20.question_text: Which numbered exit in the handbook's standard roundabout pattern reverses direction?
sec05-card-r20.teaching_text: Looping all the way around to the fourth exit reverses travel direction smoothly without risky three-point turns.

sec05-card-r21.question_text: On which half of the roadway must you normally drive?
sec05-card-r21.teaching_text: Staying on the right half separates opposing traffic streams everywhere unless a specific statutory exception applies.

sec05-card-r22.question_text: Which same-direction maneuver is a stated exception to driving on the roadway's right half?
sec05-card-r22.teaching_text: Lawful overtaking on a clear two-lane stretch temporarily uses the left half until you return right.

sec05-card-r23.question_text: How many marked lanes divide a road to create a stated exception to the right-half rule?
sec05-card-r23.teaching_text: Roads striped into three or more dedicated lanes govern position by lane markings rather than simple halves.

sec05-card-r24.question_text: What street design and posting exempts drivers from the right-half roadway rule?
sec05-card-r24.teaching_text: With zero oncoming traffic on a posted one-way street, left lanes carry legal forward flow.

sec05-card-r25.question_text: What official authority or roadside control can direct you outside the normal right half of the road?
sec05-card-r25.teaching_text: Crash scenes and construction detours routinely route vehicles left of center under officer or sign control.

sec05-card-r26.question_text: When a roadway obstruction forces you left of center, who has the right-of-way?
sec05-card-r26.teaching_text: A stalled car or fallen branch in your lane never entitles you to crowd oncoming drivers.

sec05-card-r27.question_text: How should you use the outer right lane versus the inside lane on a road with four or more lanes?
sec05-card-r27.teaching_text: Cruising in the right lane keeps the inside lane beside the divider open for passing and left turns.

sec06-card-f01.question_text: What are vehicle blind spots in relation to your interior and outside mirrors?
sec06-card-f01.teaching_text: Even well-aimed side and center mirrors leave side-quarter pockets where motorcycles or compact cars disappear.

sec06-card-f02.question_text: Which two visual checks must you combine before changing lanes?
sec06-card-f02.teaching_text: Glancing at glass alone misses cars riding beside your rear fender, so a quick head turn is essential.

sec06-card-f03.question_text: Once you spot an open lane-change gap, what sequence comes right before steering over?
sec06-card-f03.teaching_text: Traffic two lanes over can dive into the same open space while your blinker flashes, making that second look critical.

sec06-card-f04.question_text: How do you wrap up a smooth lane change once you move into the new lane?
sec06-card-f04.teaching_text: Leaving a turn signal blinking miles down the road confuses surrounding drivers into thinking another turn is coming.

sec06-card-f05.question_text: Where should your eyes check while rolling down a freeway entrance ramp toward a merge?
sec06-card-f05.teaching_text: Staring only backward over your shoulder causes classic ramp rear-enders when the merging car ahead suddenly brakes.

sec06-card-f06.question_text: How fast should you build speed in the entrance lane before merging onto a freeway, and what finishes the merge?
sec06-card-f06.teaching_text: Merging twenty miles per hour slower than highway traffic forces fast cars behind you to slam their brakes.

sec06-card-f07.question_text: How early should you position yourself in the proper lane before your highway exit?
sec06-card-f07.teaching_text: Diving across three freeway lanes at the last gore stripe triggers high-speed sideswipes and spinouts.

sec06-card-f08.question_text: When should you start slowing down for a highway exit that has a deceleration lane?
sec06-card-f08.teaching_text: Braking early on the main freeway surprises high-speed traffic behind you—save your slowing for the exit lane.

sec06-card-f09.question_text: What is the only legal move if you overshoot your freeway exit, and what median shortcut is off-limits?
sec06-card-f09.teaching_text: Paved median turnarounds are strictly reserved for patrol and emergency rigs—backing up or cutting across invites fatal hits.

sec06-card-f10.question_text: Which three directions or traffic positions must you check before pulling out to pass?
sec06-card-f10.teaching_text: Swinging left without checking behind puts you straight into the fender of a car already overtaking you.

sec06-card-f11.question_text: Once the road ahead and behind is clear, how do you move into the passing lane?
sec06-card-f11.teaching_text: Jerking abruptly across the centerline upsets stability, whereas signaling and building pace smoothly keeps full control.

sec06-card-f12.question_text: What mirror cue tells you it is safe to signal and pull back in after passing a vehicle?
sec06-card-f12.teaching_text: Pulling back right before both headlights show in your center mirror clips the passed driver's safe following gap.

sec06-card-f13.question_text: What must you do with your lane position and speed while another driver is passing you?
sec06-card-f13.teaching_text: Speeding up as someone overtakes traps them out in the opposing lane facing oncoming traffic.

sec06-card-f14.question_text: What rule applies to starting a pass when a car is coming from the opposite direction?
sec06-card-f14.teaching_text: Closing speeds double head-on, making oncoming cars reach you twice as fast as stationary landmarks suggest.

sec06-card-f15.question_text: Why is passing off-limits approaching a curve or the crest of a hill?
sec06-card-f15.teaching_text: An oncoming truck hidden just past a blind crest or bend leaves zero time or shoulder room to bail out.

sec06-card-f16.question_text: Are you allowed to pass another vehicle at an intersection?
sec06-card-f16.teaching_text: Drivers turning left ahead or pulling out from side streets never expect a passing car in the opposing lane.

sec06-card-f17.question_text: Which two narrowed or hazardous structures ahead prohibit starting a pass?
sec06-card-f17.teaching_text: Bridges strip away escape shoulders while railroad crossings hide approaching trains and sudden stops.

sec06-card-f18.question_text: On a multilane two-way road, what is the far-left travel lane meant for?
sec06-card-f18.teaching_text: Using the inside lane strictly to overtake slower cars smoothly keeps traffic flowing in both directions.

sec06-card-f19.question_text: May you ever drive onto a paved or gravel shoulder to get around traffic?
sec06-card-f19.teaching_text: Paved and unpaved shoulders collect debris, disabled cars, and cyclists—passing there is flatly illegal.

sec06-card-f20.question_text: When is crossing double solid yellow lines to pass actually permitted on an Ohio two-lane road?
sec06-card-f20.teaching_text: Ohio carves out a narrow exception letting you safely clear bicycles or orange-triangle slow-moving vehicles when sightlines open.

sec06-card-f21.question_text: Are you allowed to turn left into a private driveway across double solid yellow centerlines?
sec06-card-f21.teaching_text: Double yellow stripes ban routine overtaking, not safe left turns into driveways once oncoming lanes clear.

sec06-card-f22.question_text: When one centerline stripe is dashed yellow and the other is solid yellow, which side may pass?
sec06-card-f22.teaching_text: Look at the stripe closest to your left door: broken yellow allows passing while solid yellow locks you in.

sec06-card-f23.question_text: What is a shared center left-turn lane for, and which three uses are strictly banned inside it?
sec06-card-f23.teaching_text: Treating the center turn box as a passing chute, merge ramp, or travel lane sets up head-on collisions.

sec06-card-f24.question_text: Which two classic sign designs warn drivers of a railroad crossing?
sec06-card-f24.teaching_text: Round yellow alerts you well upstream while the white X-shaped crossbuck stands right at the tracks.

sec06-card-f25.question_text: What active train-triggered warning devices equip some railroad crossings beyond static signs?
sec06-card-f25.teaching_text: Remember that rural crossings may lack lights or gates completely, so absence of flashers never guarantees empty rails.

sec06-card-f26.question_text: How should you respond at a railroad warning sign before reaching the rails?
sec06-card-f26.teaching_text: Easing off the gas and listening lets you stop smoothly if a locomotive horn or headlight appears.

sec06-card-f27.question_text: How many feet back from a railroad crossing must you stop when a train approaches?
sec06-card-f27.teaching_text: Stopping closer than fifteen feet risks overhang hits or gate strikes, while past fifty blocks traffic needlessly.

sec06-card-r01.question_text: When may you start moving across railroad tracks after a train goes by?
sec06-card-r01.teaching_text: Driving around still-flashing red lights risks getting struck by a second train approaching on parallel rails.

sec06-card-r02.question_text: How should you approach a crossing marked only by pavement paint or a crossbuck without lights?
sec06-card-r02.teaching_text: With zero bells or gates to warn you, your own cautious approach speed is the only protection.

sec06-card-r03.question_text: Which two dangerous choices must you never make at railroad tracks?
sec06-card-r03.teaching_text: Freight trains take over a mile to stop and look slower than they travel—never race or queue on rails.
sec06-card-r03.must_match_memory_hook: Never stop on or beat trains

visual_sync.text_span: Never stop on or beat trains

sec06-card-r04.question_text: What is required of every vehicle when a stop sign is posted at a railroad crossing?
sec06-card-r04.teaching_text: Even when tracks look empty in both directions, a posted stop sign at rails mandates a complete stop.

sec06-card-r05.question_text: What do four flashing amber lights on a school bus mean, and must you stop for amber alone?
sec06-card-r05.teaching_text: Amber lights warn that red lights are seconds away—ease down now instead of hitting the gas.

sec06-card-r06.question_text: What light pattern replaces amber when a school bus stops to pick up or drop off students?
sec06-card-r06.teaching_text: Two red flashers up front and two in back signal an active student crossing zone.

sec06-card-r07.question_text: Do you still have to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights if no left-side stop arm swings out?
sec06-card-r07.teaching_text: Frozen or older bus mechanisms might not deploy a side paddle, yet flashing red lights alone mandate stopping.

sec06-card-r08.question_text: On an Ohio road with fewer than four lanes, who must stop for a school bus, how far back, and until when?
sec06-card-r08.teaching_text: Both following and oncoming traffic hold at least ten feet away until the bus rolls or the driver waves you on.

sec06-card-r09.question_text: On an Ohio road with four or more lanes, which traffic must stop for a stopped school bus?
sec06-card-r09.teaching_text: Notice Ohio's distinct four-lane rule: buses drop riders on their own curb side, so opposing lanes keep moving.

sec06-card-r10.question_text: What can a school-bus driver do if a motorist illegally passes the stopped bus?
sec06-card-r10.teaching_text: Bus drivers record license plates and locations so officers can track down and cite the driver afterward.

sec06-card-r11.question_text: Where should you park on a street, and which way must your car face?
sec06-card-r11.teaching_text: Parking nose-in against oncoming traffic requires crossing opposing lanes blindly both arriving and leaving.

sec06-card-r12.question_text: Within how many inches of the right-hand curb must you parallel park?
sec06-card-r12.teaching_text: Leaving tires farther than one foot out narrows the travel lane and risks clipped side mirrors.

sec06-card-r13.question_text: Which curb may you parallel park beside on a one-way street, and how close?
sec06-card-r13.teaching_text: Because all lanes flow one direction, Ohio allows twelve-inch parallel parking along the left or right curb.

sec06-card-r14.question_text: How are spaces meant for angled parking marked on the pavement?
sec06-card-r14.teaching_text: Centering cleanly inside diagonal stall stripes keeps doors clear and preserves backing sightlines.

sec06-card-r15.question_text: What two roadside cues should you scan for parking bans or time limits?
sec06-card-r15.teaching_text: Yellow or red curb paint and posted time plates flag tow zones even when open curb space looks inviting.

sec06-card-r16.question_text: What issued credential is required to park in a wheelchair-marked accessible space?
sec06-card-r16.teaching_text: Sitting inside with hazard flashers running for one minute still violates accessible-parking law without a placard or plate.

sec06-card-r17.question_text: When is stopping, standing, or parking on a sidewalk ever excusable?
sec06-card-r17.teaching_text: Blocking a sidewalk forces wheelchairs and strollers into street traffic unless police or conflict avoidance required stopping.

sec06-card-r18.question_text: What rule applies to stopping, standing, or parking across a public or private driveway?
sec06-card-r18.teaching_text: Even idling briefly in front of someone's apron traps residents and emergency vehicles unless traffic control directs it.

sec06-card-r19.question_text: How close to an intersection or crosswalk is stopping, standing, or parking prohibited?
sec06-card-r19.teaching_text: Parking closer than twenty feet screens pedestrians and cross-street cars from turning drivers.

sec06-card-r20.question_text: Within how many feet of a fire hydrant does Ohio ban stopping, standing, or parking?
sec06-card-r20.teaching_text: Notice Ohio's exact number is ten feet—not fifteen—giving firefighters instant hose access.

sec06-card-r21.question_text: At least how much space must you leave from another parked car when stopping, standing, or parking?
sec06-card-r21.teaching_text: Pinning another car tighter than twelve inches makes parallel exits impossible without bumper taps.

sec06-card-r22.question_text: May you stop, stand, or park out in the lane beside a car already parked at the curb?
sec06-card-r22.teaching_text: Double-parking chokes off an active travel lane and forces drivers behind you into opposing traffic.

sec06-card-r23.question_text: What rule applies where a roadside sign prohibits stopping?
sec06-card-r23.teaching_text: No-stopping zones protect rush-hour or sightline corridors where even brief passenger drop-offs are illegal.

sec06-card-r24.question_text: What four-step hill-parking sequence does the Ohio handbook give?
sec06-card-r24.teaching_text: Aiming front tires toward the curb side, shifting into park, setting the brake, and shutting off stops rollaways.

sec07-card-f01.question_text: Who violates Ohio financial-responsibility law when an uninsured car hits the road?
sec07-card-f01.teaching_text: Handing your keys to a friend without active coverage on the vehicle puts the owner on the hook too.

sec07-card-f02.question_text: Which three penalties can follow failing to show proof of insurance in Ohio?
sec07-card-f02.teaching_text: Driving uninsured triggers costly BMV reinstatement charges and loss of privileges far beyond a simple traffic fine.

sec07-card-f03.question_text: What coverage document must you show whenever an officer writes you a traffic ticket?
sec07-card-f03.teaching_text: Keeping current electronic or paper insurance proof handy avoids an automatic BMV noncompliance notice after a stop.

sec07-card-f04.question_text: What financial paperwork is checked during an Ohio vehicle-inspection stop?
sec07-card-f04.teaching_text: State troopers verify active financial responsibility right alongside lights, tires, and equipment.

sec07-card-f05.question_text: When appearing in traffic court, what coverage requirement applies every single visit?
sec07-card-f05.teaching_text: Traffic clerks check active financial responsibility at every court date, even if you already showed the officer.

sec07-card-f06.question_text: Above what dollar amount of crash property damage must a driver or owner show financial-responsibility proof?
sec07-card-f06.teaching_text: Even a minor parking-lot bumper scrape easily tops four hundred dollars and triggers mandatory insurance verification.

sec07-card-f07.question_text: How must you respond whenever the Ohio Bureau of Motor Vehicles asks for financial-responsibility proof?
sec07-card-f07.teaching_text: Ignoring a mailed BMV verification letter suspends your license even if your policy was active the whole time.

sec07-card-f08.question_text: What is Ohio's minimum liability coverage for injury or death of one person in a crash?
sec07-card-f08.teaching_text: Remember the first number in Ohio's twenty-five, fifty, twenty-five split covers bodily injury to a single victim.

sec07-card-f09.question_text: What is Ohio's minimum total liability coverage when two or more people are injured or killed?
sec07-card-f09.teaching_text: The middle fifty-thousand-dollar figure caps minimum bodily-injury payouts across everyone hurt in one crash.

sec07-card-f10.question_text: What is Ohio's minimum property-damage liability coverage per crash?
sec07-card-f10.teaching_text: That final twenty-five-thousand-dollar minimum pays for other people's damaged cars, fences, or poles—not your own car.

sec07-card-f11.question_text: Which two standard coverage instruments satisfy Ohio's minimum liability amounts?
sec07-card-f11.teaching_text: Most drivers carry an auto insurance policy, though a qualifying personal liability bond meets the same statutory minimums.

sec07-card-f12.question_text: What Registrar deposit and judgment record can substitute for an auto policy or bond?
sec07-card-f12.teaching_text: Depositing thirty thousand dollars with the Registrar only qualifies when you also prove zero unsatisfied court judgments.

sec07-card-f13.question_text: Which three record events can force you to file proof of high-risk insurance with the Bureau?
sec07-card-f13.teaching_text: Major convictions, hitting twelve points in two years, or crashing uninsured triggers mandatory state-monitored coverage filings.
sec07-card-f13.must_match_memory_hook: Serious offenses, twelve points, uninsured crash

visual_sync.text_span: Serious offenses, twelve points, uninsured crash

sec07-card-f14.question_text: What insurance promise is built into Ohio vehicle registrations and license applications?
sec07-card-f14.teaching_text: Every new, renewed, or duplicate license and plate form carries your signed pledge never to drive uninsured.

sec07-card-f15.question_text: What substance combinations make operating a vehicle illegal under Ohio impaired-driving law?
sec07-card-f15.teaching_text: Ohio OVI statutes cover drug impairment and mixed substances just as strictly as alcohol alone.

sec07-card-f16.question_text: Can doctor-prescribed pills or over-the-counter allergy and cold medicines count as impaired driving?
sec07-card-f16.teaching_text: Holding a valid doctor's prescription never excuses driving drowsy or dizzy behind the wheel.

sec07-card-f17.question_text: How do alcohol and drugs degrade your vision and spatial judgment in traffic?
sec07-card-f17.teaching_text: Losing sharp focus makes oncoming cars look farther away or slower than they really are.

sec07-card-f18.question_text: What effect do alcohol and drugs have on mental processing and driving reactions?
sec07-card-f18.teaching_text: Even a half-second delay moving your foot to the brake adds crucial car lengths at highway speed.

sec07-card-f19.question_text: How does impairment change how you read surroundings and make split-second choices?
sec07-card-f19.teaching_text: Impaired drivers miss peripheral hazards and freeze or guess wrong when traffic shifts suddenly.

sec07-card-f20.question_text: What is the legal drinking age in Ohio?
sec07-card-f20.teaching_text: Anyone younger than twenty-one faces strict underage consumption and driving thresholds across the state.

sec07-card-f21.question_text: Starting at what blood-alcohol concentration is operating a motor vehicle illegal at any age in Ohio?
sec07-card-f21.teaching_text: Remember you can still be arrested below eight hundredths of one percent whenever driving is noticeably impaired.

sec07-card-f22.question_text: What much lower blood-alcohol concentration is illegal for an Ohio driver younger than twenty-one?
sec07-card-f22.teaching_text: Two hundredths of one percent is barely a trace, meaning even part of one drink crosses the underage line.

sec07-card-f23.question_text: What two testing steps does an officer take when impaired driving or impaired physical control is suspected?
sec07-card-f23.teaching_text: Sitting behind the wheel with keys in physical control while impaired triggers the same testing authority as moving.

sec07-card-f24.question_text: Besides the officer's physical observations, which five fluid or breath samples provide impaired-driving evidence?
sec07-card-f24.teaching_text: Ohio labs test oral fluid and blood plasma alongside breath, whole blood, and urine to detect drugs or alcohol.

sec07-card-f25.question_text: What immediate action and suspension range follow a chemical test within two hours of arrest showing point zero eight or higher?
sec07-card-f25.teaching_text: Administrative license seizure happens right at arrest via sworn BMV report—months before criminal court finishes.

sec07-card-f26.question_text: What extra testing right does an arrested driver have during that over-limit suspension process, and who pays?
sec07-card-f26.teaching_text: You may request an additional private lab test to verify results, though the cost comes out of your pocket.

sec07-card-f27.question_text: What happens if you refuse a requested chemical test within two hours of an Ohio OVI arrest?
sec07-card-f27.teaching_text: Refusing triggers an immediate one-year minimum administrative suspension—four times longer than a first failed test.

sec07-card-f28.question_text: Does winning a not-guilty verdict on the impaired-driving charge cancel a chemical-test-refusal suspension?
sec07-card-f28.teaching_text: Implied-consent refusal is a separate administrative penalty that sticks even if criminal OVI charges are beat.

sec07-card-f29.question_text: What suspension span and four extra hurdles can follow operating after underage alcohol consumption?
sec07-card-f29.teaching_text: Underage OVI stacks remedial class, reinstatement fees, full license retesting, and possible jail onto the suspension.

sec07-card-f30.question_text: How many prior years does Ohio's administrative alcohol-suspension table count for past refusals or OVI convictions?
sec07-card-f30.teaching_text: Any refusal or alcohol-or-drug driving conviction inside the last decade bumps you into harsher suspension tiers.

sec07-card-f31.question_text: How long is the administrative license suspension for a first chemical-test refusal?
sec07-card-f31.teaching_text: Compare that full twelve-month refusal loss against ninety days for a first over-limit test.

sec07-card-f32.question_text: How long is the suspension for refusing a chemical test with one prior refusal or OVI conviction in ten years?
sec07-card-f32.teaching_text: Refusal penalties climb cleanly: one year first, two years with one prior, three with two, five with three-plus.

sec07-card-f33.question_text: What suspension hits if you refuse a chemical test with two prior refusals or OVI convictions in ten years?
sec07-card-f33.teaching_text: Having two prior events inside ten years triples the first-time refusal suspension up to three full years.

sec07-card-f34.question_text: How long is the license suspension for refusing a chemical test with three or more priors in ten years?
sec07-card-f34.teaching_text: Three or more prior refusals or convictions max out the administrative refusal schedule at five years.

sec07-card-r01.question_text: How long is the administrative suspension for a first over-limit chemical test?
sec07-card-r01.teaching_text: Testing over the limit with a clean ten-year record brings a three-month, ninety-day administrative suspension.

sec07-card-r02.question_text: How long is an over-limit test suspension when you have one prior OVI or drug conviction in ten years?
sec07-card-r02.teaching_text: Notice each over-limit tier sits one step below the refusal ladder: ninety days, then one, two, and three years.

sec07-card-r03.question_text: What administrative suspension follows an over-limit test with two prior OVI or drug convictions in ten years?
sec07-card-r03.teaching_text: With two prior convictions on the ten-year clock, failing a chemical test triggers a two-year administrative loss.

sec07-card-r04.question_text: How long is the administrative suspension for an over-limit test with three or more prior convictions in ten years?
sec07-card-r04.teaching_text: Three or more ten-year priors push an administrative failed-test suspension to three full years before criminal sentencing.

sec07-card-r05.question_text: How many impaired-driving convictions within twenty years place a driver on Ohio's habitual offender registry, and what else follows?
sec07-card-r05.teaching_text: Reaching five OVI convictions in twenty years brings jail, public habitual-offender listing, and possible vehicle forfeiture.

sec07-card-r06.question_text: What should you do before driving after taking an over-the-counter medication?
sec07-card-r06.teaching_text: Common allergy, cold, or motion-sickness tablets cause heavy drowsiness that mimics alcohol behind the wheel.

sec07-card-r07.question_text: Which four prescription drug types specifically warn of driving side effects you should check with a doctor or pharmacist?
sec07-card-r07.teaching_text: Calming, sleep, mood, and pain prescriptions slow reaction times dramatically, especially during the first doses.

sec07-card-r08.question_text: Which four driving abilities do illegal drugs harm, and what is the rule on driving with them?
sec07-card-r08.teaching_text: Illicit stimulants, hallucinogens, and depressants distort reflexes, judgment, sight, and alertness unpredictably.

sec07-card-r09.question_text: Why must you never combine alcohol with other impairing medications or drugs?
sec07-card-r09.teaching_text: One pill plus one drink does not just add up—chemical synergy multiplies sedation and coordination loss.

sec07-card-r10.question_text: Who assigns Ohio license penalty points, and what determines how many points you get?
sec07-card-r10.teaching_text: Convicting courts assess statutory point values scaled to the severity of the violation and repeat history.

sec07-card-r11.question_text: What happens when an Ohio driver reaches six penalty points within a two-year window?
sec07-card-r11.teaching_text: Reaching six points puts you halfway to suspension and prompts an official BMV warning letter.

sec07-card-r12.question_text: How many penalty points accumulated within two years trigger an Ohio license suspension?
sec07-card-r12.teaching_text: Stacking twelve or more points inside any twenty-four-month span suspends your driving privileges.

sec07-card-r13.question_text: Which steps are included to reinstate your license after a twelve-point suspension?
sec07-card-r13.teaching_text: Waiting out the calendar time alone is not enough—you must finish remedial training, file proof, and pay fees.

sec07-card-r14.question_text: Is an SR-22 a separate insurance policy, or what is it actually?
sec07-card-r14.teaching_text: Test distractors call SR-22 high-risk insurance itself, when it is actually a state filing certificate from your insurer.

sec07-card-r15.question_text: How many points are assigned to ordinary moving violations, certain speeding tickets, and license-restriction violations?
sec07-card-r15.teaching_text: Most everyday traffic tickets and breaking a corrective-lens or curfew restriction add two points apiece.

sec07-card-r16.question_text: How many penalty points does willful or wanton disregard for safety carry in Ohio?
sec07-card-r16.teaching_text: Reckless driving hits twice as hard as an ordinary moving ticket, stacking four points at once.

sec07-card-r17.question_text: How many penalty points hit your record for failing to stop and give your identity after a crash?
sec07-card-r17.teaching_text: Leaving a crash scene drops six points at once—triggering a warning letter immediately and putting you halfway to suspension.

sec07-card-r18.question_text: What happens if an Ohio driver under eighteen gets two moving-violation convictions or guilty pleas?
sec07-card-r18.teaching_text: Teens do not get twelve points of leeway—just two moving tickets before eighteen suspend privileges automatically for ninety days.

sec07-card-r19.question_text: What automatic suspension hits an Ohio driver under eighteen convicted of three moving violations?
sec07-card-r19.teaching_text: A third moving ticket before your eighteenth birthday quadruples the suspension to one full year.

sec07-card-r20.question_text: How long is the license suspension for an under-eighteen driver convicted of probationary impaired operation?
sec07-card-r20.teaching_text: A juvenile impaired-driving conviction or guilty plea sidelines a probationary teen driver for half a year.

sec07-card-r21.question_text: Which three steps are required to reinstate after an under-eighteen probationary suspension?
sec07-card-r21.teaching_text: Suspended probationary teens essentially restart from a temporary permit, finish juvenile improvement class, and retake the road test.
sec07-card-r21.must_match_memory_hook: New permit, juvenile course, road test

visual_sync.text_span: New permit, juvenile course, road test

sec07-card-r22.question_text: What misdemeanor level, maximum fine, and extra suspension can follow driving on a suspended Ohio license?
sec07-card-r22.teaching_text: Getting caught behind the wheel while suspended is a serious crime carrying up to a thousand-dollar fine and another year off.

sec07-card-r23.question_text: What risk does a vehicle owner take by knowingly letting a suspended driver borrow their car?
sec07-card-r23.teaching_text: Knowingly handing keys to someone with a suspended license exposes the car owner to the exact same criminal penalties.

sec07-card-r24.question_text: What is Ohio's rule on clinging to or riding on the outside of a moving motor vehicle?
sec07-card-r24.teaching_text: Skitching, hood-surfing, or hanging onto bumpers turns a slight tap of the brakes into a fatal fall.

sec07-card-r25.question_text: Below what age and above what speed is riding in an open truck or trailer cargo bed generally banned?
sec07-card-r25.teaching_text: Unroofed pickup beds offer zero ejection protection once speeds pass twenty-five miles per hour.

sec07-card-r26.question_text: What seating and belt setup creates an exception to the open-cargo-bed rule?
sec07-card-r26.teaching_text: Only a properly anchored seat paired with a safety belt meeting federal restraint standards qualifies.

sec07-card-r27.question_text: What urgent situation creates an exception to the open-cargo-area riding ban?
sec07-card-r27.teaching_text: Evacuating someone during a genuine life-threatening emergency excuses riding in an open cargo bed.

sec07-card-r28.question_text: Which workers are exempt from the open-cargo-area riding restriction?
sec07-card-r28.teaching_text: Crews placing cones or maintaining highways under public-agency authority may work from open utility beds.

sec07-card-r29.question_text: What safety standard and instruction rule govern every child safety seat you use?
sec07-card-r29.teaching_text: Even a top-rated federally compliant car seat fails in a crash if strapped loosely against manufacturer rules.

sec07-card-r30.question_text: Where must you never install a rear-facing infant or child safety seat?
sec07-card-r30.teaching_text: A deploying front airbag strikes the back of a rear-facing shell right behind the infant's head with lethal force.

sec07-card-r31.question_text: Which age or weight thresholds require a child to ride in a federally compliant child safety seat in Ohio?
sec07-card-r31.teaching_text: Notice it is an either-or rule: a three-year-old over forty pounds OR a four-year-old at thirty-six pounds still needs a car seat.

sec07-card-r32.question_text: In Ohio, which children aged four through seven must use a booster seat, and what height lets them graduate?
sec07-card-r32.teaching_text: Boosters lift smaller kids so adult lap-and-shoulder belts cross strong hip and collarbone bones instead of the belly and neck.

sec07-card-r33.question_text: Which older-child age span requires safety-belt use under Ohio's child-restraint section?
sec07-card-r33.teaching_text: Once children outgrow boosters at age eight or four-foot-nine, safety belts remain mandatory all the way through fifteen.

sec07-card-r34.question_text: Through what age does the handbook advise keeping children in the back seat away from front airbags?
sec07-card-r34.teaching_text: Front airbags inflate at speeds calibrated for adult frames, making the back seat far safer through age twelve.

sec07-card-r35.question_text: Which three vehicle categories are listed as exempt from Ohio's child-restraint requirements?
sec07-card-r35.teaching_text: Patrol or emergency units, taxicabs, and vintage cars built before federal seat-belt mandates fall outside the car-seat statute.

sec07-card-r36.question_text: Which two instruction booklets should you read before strapping in a child restraint?
sec07-card-r36.teaching_text: Your vehicle manual shows exact LATCH anchor spots and tether hooks while the seat booklet covers harness routing.

sec08-card-f01.question_text: When police signal you to pull over, how and where should you bring your vehicle to a stop?
sec08-card-f01.teaching_text: Signaling promptly shows the officer you noticed their lights while guiding you smoothly onto the right shoulder or nearest safe spot.

sec08-card-f02.question_text: Once stopped during a police traffic stop, what gear and engine steps secure your car?
sec08-card-f02.teaching_text: Placing the transmission in park and shutting off the ignition prevents accidental forward creep while the officer approaches.

sec08-card-f03.question_text: At a traffic stop, what should you do with your window — and should you step out of the vehicle?
sec08-card-f03.teaching_text: Opening a door uninvited alarms approaching officers and puts you inches from fast passing traffic.

sec08-card-f04.question_text: What demeanor and seat-belt rule apply while you wait during a police stop?
sec08-card-f04.teaching_text: Unbuckling early looks like rummaging inside the cabin and strips away crash protection if a passing car drifts onto the shoulder.

sec08-card-f05.question_text: Where should both of your hands stay during a police traffic stop?
sec08-card-f05.teaching_text: Resting both hands in plain view on the steering wheel reassures the officer before anyone reaches into pockets or gloveboxes.

sec08-card-f06.question_text: When does the Ohio manual advise telling an officer if any weapons are inside your vehicle?
sec08-card-f06.teaching_text: Sharing that information calmly right when the officer greets you prevents dangerous misunderstandings later in the stop.

sec08-card-f07.question_text: How should you respond to an officer's directions throughout a traffic stop?
sec08-card-f07.teaching_text: Waiting for and following clear directions keeps roadside stops predictable and safe for everyone involved.

sec08-card-f08.question_text: Which three documents or credentials must you hand over when requested at a traffic stop?
sec08-card-f08.teaching_text: Waiting until the officer asks before reaching for those three items avoids sudden hand movements as they walk up.

sec08-card-f09.question_text: How should you interact with the officer during a stop, and what if an instruction seems unclear?
sec08-card-f09.teaching_text: Roadside shoulders are never the place to debate traffic law, though polite clarifying questions keep you compliant.

sec08-card-f10.question_text: Where may a driver contest a traffic ticket if they disagree with it?
sec08-card-f10.teaching_text: Traffic court gives you a formal, safe forum to present your side instead of escalating tension on the shoulder.

sec08-card-f11.question_text: During which daily sun-to-sun timeframe must Ohio drivers keep vehicle lights on?
sec08-card-f11.teaching_text: Switching headlamps on right at sunset covers dim twilight when unlit cars vanish against dark pavement.

sec08-card-f12.question_text: At what hours must you turn on vehicle lights during rain, snow, fog, or other poor atmospheric conditions?
sec08-card-f12.teaching_text: Even bright midday fog or snow squalls swallow unlit vehicles unless front and rear lamps glow.

sec08-card-f13.question_text: At what forward visibility distance does limited natural light require turning on your vehicle's lights?
sec08-card-f13.teaching_text: Whenever heavy clouds, dusk, or haze blur objects inside one thousand feet, Ohio law mandates full lights.

sec08-card-f14.question_text: What lighting rule triggers in Ohio whenever rain, snow, or sleet requires running your windshield wipers?
sec08-card-f14.teaching_text: Tying your headlight switch directly to your wiper stalk guarantees trailing cars spot your taillights in spray.

sec08-card-f15.question_text: What sets the limit on how far ahead a driver can see after dark?
sec08-card-f15.teaching_text: Outside city streetlights, hazards remain invisible until they enter the cone lit by your headlamps.

sec08-card-f16.question_text: What kind of speed choice should govern your driving after dark?
sec08-card-f16.teaching_text: Dialing speed back at night keeps your stopping distance tucked safely inside your illuminated beam cone.

sec08-card-f17.question_text: When should you use high-beam headlights at night, and when must you dim them?
sec08-card-f17.teaching_text: High beams stretch sightlines on empty stretches, but dimming promptly keeps oncoming drivers from going glare-blind.

sec08-card-f18.question_text: Where should you aim your eyes when an approaching vehicle shines bright headlights toward you?
sec08-card-f18.teaching_text: Watching the right pavement edge guides your lane position while sparing your eyes temporary glare blindness.

sec08-card-f19.question_text: Why should you glance briefly toward each side of the road from time to time at night?
sec08-card-f19.teaching_text: Occasional side sweeps spot pavement drop-offs, deer, or pedestrians before they cross into your beam cone.

sec08-card-r01.question_text: Why shouldn't you wear tinted glasses or sunglasses after dark or under gray overcast skies?
sec08-card-r01.teaching_text: Dark or tinted glasses filter out faint contrast needed to spot pedestrians and unlit hazards in low light.

sec08-card-r02.question_text: How should you manage speed, following distance, and stopping readiness when driving in fog?
sec08-card-r02.teaching_text: Queued traffic can appear out of thick mist without warning, demanding steady cushions and instant brake readiness.

sec08-card-r03.question_text: Which headlight setting belongs in fog instead of high beams, and what visual habit goes with it?
sec08-card-r03.teaching_text: High beams reflect blinding white glare off fog droplets, whereas low beams cut underneath while you scan ahead.

sec08-card-r04.question_text: How should you use your eyes while driving through fog rather than fixing on a single spot?
sec08-card-r04.teaching_text: Staring rigidly into gray mist hypnotizes depth judgment and misses faint brake glow off to the side.

sec08-card-r05.question_text: What should you do right after a foggy-weather crash if your car still drives — or if it cannot move?
sec08-card-r05.teaching_text: Getting off live lanes prevents chain pileups, and lights, flashers, plus flares warn approaching drivers if disabled.

sec08-card-r06.question_text: How must your speed change for winter driving, particularly on snow-covered or icy roads?
sec08-card-r06.teaching_text: Slower winter speeds keep steering and braking forces below the low-grip threshold where tires break loose.

sec08-card-r07.question_text: Why must you leave a wider cushion behind vehicles ahead on winter or slick roads?
sec08-card-r07.teaching_text: Packed snow and ice multiply braking runs, turning normal dry-weather following gaps into rear-end traps.

sec08-card-r08.question_text: Which three highway locations ice over before ordinary flat road sections?
sec08-card-r08.teaching_text: Exposed bridge decks lose heat from underneath while tree shade blocks winter sun from melting frost.

sec08-card-r09.question_text: What gentle pedal technique does the Ohio manual describe to shed momentum without losing winter grip?
sec08-card-r09.teaching_text: Light brake taps trim speed gradually on slick roads without shocking tires into a locked slide.

sec08-card-r10.question_text: If your vehicle starts skidding, what three accelerator, steering, and brake rules apply?
sec08-card-r10.teaching_text: Touching the brakes mid-skid locks sliding wheels worse, whereas steering in the skid's direction restores rolling control.

sec08-card-r11.question_text: Which three changing traffic or equipment features may wait inside a highway work zone?
sec08-card-r11.teaching_text: Expecting lane shifts, temporary detours, and heavy trucks pulling in and out keeps you alert through roadwork.

sec08-card-r12.question_text: Which five roadside markers, vehicles, or people must you scan for when nearing a work zone?
sec08-card-r12.teaching_text: Spotting orange signs and barrels early gives you room to merge smoothly before flaggers and crews appear.

sec08-card-r13.question_text: What background and legend colors identify Ohio work-zone warning signs?
sec08-card-r13.teaching_text: Bright orange diamonds and rectangles alert you immediately that temporary construction rules replace normal patterns.

sec08-card-r14.question_text: Why must you still slow down through a work zone even when no workers are on site?
sec08-card-r14.teaching_text: Chipped pavement lips, grooved asphalt, and tight concrete barriers stay dangerous overnight and on weekends.

sec09-card-f01.question_text: Why should you use a consistent visual search pattern every time you drive?
sec09-card-f01.teaching_text: Systematic eye sweeps catch developing conflicts while you still have room to ease speed or shift lanes.

sec09-card-f02.question_text: Ideally, how many seconds ahead along your intended route should you scan in Ohio?
sec09-card-f02.teaching_text: Ohio's twenty-to-thirty-second visual lead gives you twice the planning horizon of drivers staring just ahead of their hood.

sec09-card-f03.question_text: What hazards do side glances catch, and how do you check blind spots toward the rear?
sec09-card-f03.teaching_text: Sweeping cross-traffic points plus looking over your shoulder covers zones outside forward sightlines and flat mirrors.

sec09-card-f04.question_text: Before which four common driving actions is checking rear traffic in your mirrors especially critical?
sec09-card-f04.teaching_text: Glancing at mirrors before braking or entering intersections warns you if a distracted tailgater is closing too fast.

sec09-card-f05.question_text: How should you balance road conditions, following distance, and legal limits when managing speed?
sec09-card-f05.teaching_text: Safe pacing adapts down for traffic or weather while preserving forward space and never topping posted signs.

sec09-card-f06.question_text: When should you slow down for a curve, and what throttle feel should that entry speed allow through the bend?
sec09-card-f06.teaching_text: Shedding speed on the straight approach lets light, steady acceleration settle your tires smoothly around the arc.

sec09-card-f07.question_text: Which three traction, traffic, or sightline conditions call for slowing down even further at a curve?
sec09-card-f07.teaching_text: A blind curve exit can hide a stalled car or sharp tightening radius right beyond the bend.

sec09-card-f08.question_text: When should you begin reducing speed as rain, snow, sleet, or ice starts?
sec09-card-f08.teaching_text: Waiting until tires slip to back off the gas is too late because early precipitation turns pavement greasy immediately.

sec09-card-f09.question_text: What two stopping and cornering penalties result from reduced tire grip on slick pavement?
sec09-card-f09.teaching_text: Lower friction means brakes need extra road to halt and sharp steering inputs break sideways into skids.

sec09-card-f10.question_text: In Ohio's safe-driving chapter, what gentle gas and brake inputs are described when a car starts to slide?
sec09-card-f10.teaching_text: Slowly lifting off the accelerator and applying light, smooth brake pressure avoids jolting sliding tires.

sec09-card-f11.question_text: What twin speed and spacing adjustments belong on wet, snowy, or icy roads?
sec09-card-f11.teaching_text: Pairing lower speed with a longer gap ahead buys stopping room when slick asphalt stretches braking distance.

sec09-card-f12.question_text: What happens to your front steering tires when hydroplaning occurs?
sec09-card-f12.teaching_text: Once water lifts the front treads off the asphalt, turning the steering wheel produces almost zero direction change.

sec09-card-f13.question_text: How do you cut the risk of hydroplaning in rain or where puddles collect on wet roads?
sec09-card-f13.teaching_text: Dropping speed lets tire tread grooves channel standing rainwater away instead of planing up on top.

sec09-card-f14.question_text: What should you do with the accelerator if your vehicle begins hydroplaning?
sec09-card-f14.teaching_text: Gradually lifting off the gas lets your tires slow down smoothly until they sink back onto firm pavement.

sec09-card-f15.question_text: How should you handle a large stretch of standing floodwater across the road?
sec09-card-f15.teaching_text: Deep puddles hide stalled-engine depth and washed-out roadbeds, so turn around and pick an alternate route.

sec09-card-f16.question_text: What is a space cushion around your vehicle, and what advantage does it give you?
sec09-card-f16.teaching_text: Keeping clear distance between your bumpers and surrounding road users buys time to steer or brake smoothly.

sec09-card-f17.question_text: From what mental moment to what final state does total stopping distance measure your car's travel?
sec09-card-f17.teaching_text: Total stopping distance counts every foot rolled during perception, foot movement, and actual braking.

sec09-card-f18.question_text: How does faster travel speed change the time and distance needed to stop?
sec09-card-f18.teaching_text: Kinetic energy climbs rapidly with speed, demanding both more seconds and far more pavement to halt.

sec09-card-f19.question_text: What does perception time measure, and how long does it average for an alert driver?
sec09-card-f19.teaching_text: Even wide-awake eyes burn nearly a full second just realizing brake lights ahead mean trouble.

sec09-card-f20.question_text: What movement does reaction time cover, and what is the stated average duration?
sec09-card-f20.teaching_text: Shifting your right shoe from throttle to brake pedal adds another three-quarters to one full second before pads bite.

sec09-card-f21.question_text: Traveling fifty miles per hour with sound brakes on dry asphalt, roughly how many feet can mechanical braking require?
sec09-card-f21.teaching_text: That one hundred fifty-eight feet covers mechanical braking alone — on top of distance rolled during perception and reaction.

sec09-card-f22.question_text: What two minimum forward-spacing rules — one by car lengths and one by seconds — does Ohio recommend?
sec09-card-f22.teaching_text: Know both benchmarks for exam day — one car length per ten miles per hour or a four-second count.

sec09-card-f23.question_text: How do you use a fixed roadside object to count your following interval behind a lead vehicle?
sec09-card-f23.teaching_text: Timing from the lead rear bumper passing a sign or shadow until your front arrives works at any speed.

sec09-card-f24.question_text: Under Ohio's timed-interval method, what does reaching the landmark before four seconds mean?
sec09-card-f24.teaching_text: Arriving in two or three seconds leaves too little reaction buffer under Ohio's four-second standard.

sec09-card-f25.question_text: If your landmark count comes up shorter than four seconds, how should you correct and verify it?
sec09-card-f25.teaching_text: Backing off slightly and timing again at the next pole confirms you restored at least four full seconds.

sec09-card-f26.question_text: What simple counting exercise helps sharpen your ability to judge travel seconds ahead?
sec09-card-f26.teaching_text: Predicting how many seconds away a bridge or sign sits and counting it out calibrates your eyes fast.

sec09-card-f27.question_text: How should you adjust forward spacing after dark or when weather cuts visibility?
sec09-card-f27.teaching_text: When darkness, rain, or fog hides brake lights until closer, extra seconds ahead restore lost reaction margin.

sec09-card-f28.question_text: How must your following distance change whenever pavement turns slippery?
sec09-card-f28.teaching_text: Wet, icy, or slushy asphalt needs longer braking runs even with fresh tires and antilock brakes.

sec09-card-f29.question_text: Behind which four large or towing vehicle categories should you open a wider following gap?
sec09-card-f29.teaching_text: Wide trucks, buses, RVs, and towed trailers block your forward view unless you hang farther back.

sec09-card-f30.question_text: Why must you keep extra room behind buses and hazardous-material carriers near railroad crossings?
sec09-card-f30.teaching_text: Buses and placarded hazmat haulers must stop at railroad tracks even when crossing lights stay off.

sec09-card-r01.question_text: What crash-avoidance option does keeping open space beside your vehicle give you?
sec09-card-r01.teaching_text: When forward braking alone cannot prevent contact, an open lane or shoulder beside you offers an escape path.

sec09-card-r02.question_text: Why is cruising right next to another vehicle for long stretches dangerous?
sec09-card-r02.teaching_text: Pacing beside someone parks you inside their blind spot while walling off your own side escape route.

sec09-card-r03.question_text: How should you position your vehicle relative to the centerline and oncoming traffic?
sec09-card-r03.teaching_text: Drifting close to the yellow centerline leaves zero margin if an oncoming driver wanders wide.

sec09-card-r04.question_text: What two adjustments help entering drivers merge onto a multilane or limited-access highway?
sec09-card-r04.teaching_text: Moving over a lane when clear — or easing speed slightly — opens a clean pocket for ramp traffic.

sec09-card-r05.question_text: Which vulnerable road users — especially young ones — deserve extra side clearance?
sec09-card-r05.teaching_text: Children dart unpredictably near curbs and bicyclists swerve around grates or potholes without warning.

sec09-card-r06.question_text: Where inside your own lane should you ease when a tractor-trailer overtakes you?
sec09-card-r06.teaching_text: Shifting slightly toward the outer edge of your lane adds buffer against wind buffeting and wide trailer sway.

sec09-card-r07.question_text: What three habits help drivers behind you maintain a safe following gap?
sec09-card-r07.teaching_text: Holding steady speed, signaling early, and opening extra front room let you brake gradually before turning.

sec09-card-r08.question_text: Which three darkness, visibility, or wiper situations call for turning on headlights to communicate your presence?
sec09-card-r08.teaching_text: Running lights at night, in haze, and whenever wipers sweep rain helps other drivers spot your car early.

sec09-card-r09.question_text: When headlights are needed, what traffic situation bars using high beams?
sec09-card-r09.teaching_text: High beams help illuminate empty dark stretches, yet oncoming windshields require immediate low beams.

sec09-card-r10.question_text: Which three situations justify a light tap on the horn to get someone's attention?
sec09-card-r10.teaching_text: A polite horn tap alerts approaching cyclists or walkers, lane-drifting cars mid-pass, or distracted drivers.

sec09-card-r11.question_text: Why must you reserve your horn strictly for necessary safety warnings?
sec09-card-r11.teaching_text: Laying on the horn out of impatience can startle a cyclist into swerving or spark road rage.

sec09-card-r12.question_text: Before which three directional moves must you signal so surrounding traffic has time to react?
sec09-card-r12.teaching_text: Blinking ahead of every lane shift, highway merge, and corner turn prevents surprise conflicts.

sec09-card-r13.question_text: At least how many feet before your turn must you switch on your turn signal in Ohio?
sec09-card-r13.teaching_text: Flipping your signal on right as you crank the wheel gives zero warning — start at least one hundred feet back.

sec09-card-r14.question_text: Why should you verify your turn signal switches off right after finishing a turn or lane change?
sec09-card-r14.teaching_text: A forgotten flashing signal can trick cross-street drivers into pulling straight out in front of you.

sec09-card-r15.question_text: What message do your red brake lights send to road users behind you?
sec09-card-r15.teaching_text: Illuminated brake lamps alert trailing drivers immediately to lift off the gas and preserve space.

sec09-card-r16.question_text: In which turning or parking situations is signaling BEFORE you start slowing down critical?
sec09-card-r16.teaching_text: Without a turn lane, signaling before braking explains why you are slowing mid-block or before an intersection.

sec09-card-r17.question_text: What absolute rule applies to leaving children unattended inside or around vehicles?
sec09-card-r17.teaching_text: Parked cabins heat up lethally fast, and unattended children around driveways risk rollaway or backover tragedies.

sec09-card-r18.question_text: What quick visual habit should you practice every single time before locking your parked vehicle?
sec09-card-r18.teaching_text: Looking into the rear row every trip catches a sleeping infant even when your daily routine changes.

sec09-card-r19.question_text: What can you place in the back seat when driving so you never forget to open the rear door on arrival?
sec09-card-r19.teaching_text: Setting your work bag, purse, or lunch in the back row guarantees you open the rear door upon parking.

sec09-card-r20.question_text: How can a stuffed animal placed on the front passenger seat prevent hot-car tragedies?
sec09-card-r20.teaching_text: Moving a plush toy from the car seat up front whenever a child rides gives an unmistakable visual cue.

sec09-card-r21.question_text: What communication backup should parents arrange with their childcare provider?
sec09-card-r21.teaching_text: A prompt call when a child misses morning drop-off catches schedule mix-ups between parents within minutes.

sec09-card-r22.question_text: Why should you — along with neighbors and caregivers — keep parked car doors and trunks locked all year?
sec09-card-r22.teaching_text: Curious kids climb into unlocked cars or trunks while playing and can get trapped inside quickly.

sec09-card-r23.question_text: If a child goes missing, why must searchers check inside nearby car cabins and trunks even when doors are locked?
sec09-card-r23.teaching_text: A child who climbed inside an unlocked car may accidentally hit the interior lock button and trap themselves.

sec09-card-r24.question_text: What three immediate steps should you take if you spot a child left alone inside a parked vehicle?
sec09-card-r24.teaching_text: Dialing nine one one immediately while testing door handles and paging nearby stores saves critical minutes.

sec09-card-r25.question_text: What action does the Ohio manual direct if a child trapped inside a car looks distressed or unresponsive?
sec09-card-r25.teaching_text: Heatstroke turns life-threatening in minutes, so get an unresponsive or distressed child out immediately — breaking glass if locked.

sec09-card-r26.question_text: What must you do once a child is rescued from a hot vehicle while emergency responders are on the way?
sec09-card-r26.teaching_text: Remaining right with the child lets you monitor breathing and guide paramedics the moment they arrive.

sec09-card-r27.question_text: Why must you never leave pets inside a parked car — even with the windows cracked?
sec09-card-r27.teaching_text: Even with cracked windows, cabin heat can spike twenty degrees Fahrenheit in just ten minutes.

sec10-card-f01.question_text: Why must drivers stay alert and yield to pedestrians even outside marked crosswalks or against walk signals?
sec10-card-f01.teaching_text: Pedestrians have zero crash protection, so right-of-way rules never excuse striking someone jaywalking or hard to spot.

sec10-card-f02.question_text: Which pedestrians carry special visual-aid cues that automatically give them the right-of-way?
sec10-card-f02.teaching_text: Never honk or edge forward around a person using a white cane or service dog—stop completely until clear.

sec10-card-f03.question_text: Who holds priority when your vehicle turns across a crosswalk where pedestrians are walking?
sec10-card-f03.teaching_text: Staring left for a traffic gap while turning right is a classic trap that blinds drivers to curb pedestrians.

sec10-card-f04.question_text: Why do pedestrians near parked cars or stopped buses call for extra caution?
sec10-card-f04.teaching_text: Tall SUVs, delivery vans, and stopped transit buses screen adults and children until they step into live traffic.

sec10-card-f05.question_text: What check must you perform behind your vehicle before shifting into reverse and backing up?
sec10-card-f05.teaching_text: Rear pillars and trunk lids create a deep low blind zone right behind the bumper where children can stand.

sec10-card-f06.question_text: How should you adjust your mindset and readiness near playgrounds and neighborhood streets?
sec10-card-f06.teaching_text: Children chasing balls or pets focus on play rather than traffic, darting between driveways with zero warning.

sec10-card-f07.question_text: When must you drop to Ohio's school-zone speed limit, and whose directions govern school crossings?
sec10-card-f07.teaching_text: Slowing for active beacons or visible students—and halting whenever a guard signals—protects crowded arrival and dismissal zones.

sec10-card-f08.question_text: How do a motorcyclist's legal road rights and duties compare with those of a car driver?
sec10-card-f08.teaching_text: A narrow two-wheeled silhouette hides easily behind windshield pillars and traffic, yet carries full vehicle lane rights.

sec10-card-f09.question_text: How much of a traffic lane belongs to a motorcycle riding ahead of or beside you?
sec10-card-f09.teaching_text: Never crowd into a rider's lane, because motorcyclists use every foot of width to dodge wind gusts and debris.

sec10-card-f10.question_text: Why must you actively look for motorcycles during mirror glances and over-the-shoulder blind-spot checks?
sec10-card-f10.teaching_text: Compact bikes slip completely inside side-mirror dead zones where a quick glance tuned only for wide cars misses them.

sec10-card-f11.question_text: According to the Ohio handbook, how does a motorcycle's stopping distance compare with that of passenger cars?
sec10-card-f11.teaching_text: Remember the specific Ohio handbook rule that braking hard on two wheels takes extra stopping distance compared with cars.

sec10-card-f12.question_text: Why is it risky to pull out in front of an approaching motorcycle just because its turn signal is blinking?
sec10-card-f12.teaching_text: Many motorcycle turn signals do not self-cancel after a previous lane change, setting up deadly left-turn T-bones.

sec10-card-f13.question_text: What minimum following gap should you keep behind a motorcycle at low speed in ideal conditions?
sec10-card-f13.teaching_text: Even on dry pavement at city speeds, riders can downshift without brake lights or swerve quickly.

sec10-card-f14.question_text: To how many seconds should you expand your following gap behind a motorcycle in fast, wet, dark, heavy, unfamiliar, or tired driving?
sec10-card-f14.teaching_text: Adding at least an extra second at highway speed or in rain gives crucial space if a rider goes down.

sec10-card-f15.question_text: Why might a motorcyclist suddenly slow down or shift position within their lane?
sec10-card-f15.teaching_text: Minor road flaws that a four-wheeled car rolls right over—like loose gravel, wet steel rails, or grooves—can upset two wheels.

sec10-card-f16.question_text: How does Ohio law classify a bicycle on the street, and which direction must it ride?
sec10-card-f16.teaching_text: Riding with traffic rather than facing oncoming cars keeps closing speeds lower and puts cyclists where turning drivers look.

sec10-card-f17.question_text: What traffic controls and road rules apply to bicyclists riding on Ohio roadways?
sec10-card-f17.teaching_text: Stop signs, red lights, and turn-lane markings govern bicycles on the street just like motor vehicles.

sec10-card-f18.question_text: What speed adjustment should you make as you approach or overtake a cyclist?
sec10-card-f18.teaching_text: Blasting past at full speed creates a turbulent wind wash that can pull a lightweight bicycle off balance.

sec10-card-f19.question_text: Why should you avoid honking your horn right next to or behind a bicyclist?
sec10-card-f19.teaching_text: A sudden loud horn blast feet away can startle a cyclist into swerving straight into your vehicle.

sec10-card-f20.question_text: When is it appropriate to overtake a bicyclist sharing the roadway ahead?
sec10-card-f20.teaching_text: Holding back a few seconds behind a cyclist on a blind bend beats squeezing between oncoming cars and handlebars.

sec10-card-r01.question_text: What is the minimum side clearance Ohio requires between your motor vehicle and a bicycle?
sec10-card-r01.teaching_text: Three feet of lateral air space buffers cyclists against mirror clips, wind gusts, and minor pothole wobbles.

sec10-card-r02.question_text: What turning mistake around a cyclist must you avoid after passing or approaching a corner?
